title: BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT and AD HOC COMMITTEE FOR LA RECOVERY REPORT relative to the formation of a Pacific Palisades Disaster Recovery District…
text:
[Council File 25-0006-S38; CD 11]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
BUDGET AND FINANCE COMMITTEE REPORT and AD HOC COMMITTEE FOR LA RECOVERY REPORT relative to the formation of a Pacific Palisades Disaster Recovery District (DRD) to support efforts within the Palisades Fire Disaster Area. A. Budget and Finance Committee Report Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. COMMIT no more than 50 percent of the City’s share of the tax increment from the DRD for a term of up to 25 years, with the final percentage and term to be approved by the City Council when it considers the Infrastructure Financing Plan (IFP) that includes the prioritized list of projects to be funded by the DRD.
2. INSTRUCT the City Administrative Officer (CAO) and the Community Investment Department (CID) to request the County of Los Angeles (County) to participate in the DRD and negotiate the terms of the participation, including the percentage of the tax increment contribution, the duration of the DRD, the addition of projects to the prioritized list, and the composition of the Public Financing Authority (PFA).
3. INSTRUCT the CID, with the assistance of the City Attorney and the CAO, to prepare a Resolution of Intention (ROI) for potential consideration and adoption by the City Council to form the DRD, contingent upon County participation, that includes all of the following:
a. State that a district is proposed to be established under Government Code Section 62313 and describe the boundaries of the proposed district.
b. State the type of public facilities and development proposed to be financed or assisted by the district in accordance with State law.
c. State the need for the district and the goals the district proposes to achieve.
d. State that incremental property tax revenue from the City within the district, if approved by resolution pursuant to Section 53398.68, may be used to finance these activities.
e. Fix a time and place for the public meeting on the proposal.
f. Establish the PFA to act as the governing board of the DRD to be initially comprised of the Mayor, two Councilmembers, and two members of the public appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by the City Council; the composition of the PFA shall be revised in accordance with Government Code Section 53398.51.1 to include County representatives upon County participation in the DRD.
g. Ensure the PFA prepares an annual report in accordance with Government Code Section 53398.66, including project description and progress, actual and budgeted revenues and expenses, amount of tax increment revenues received, and an assessment of the status regarding completion of the DRD projects.
4. INSTRUCT the City Clerk to post notice of the meeting (must be held on or earlier than January 6, 2027) to consider the ROI in the City’s website at least ten days before the meeting. The notice shall do all of the following:
a. Describe specifically the boundaries of the proposed area.
b. Describe the purpose of the IFP.
c. State the day, hour, and place when and where the public can inspect documents related to the DRD.
5. INSTRUCT the CAO, in coordination with the County and with the assistance of Bureau of Engineering and other relevant departments, to prepare a prioritized list of projects to be funded by the DRD, for Council consideration within one year from the adoption of the ROI, with said projects:
a. Focused on rebuilding public infrastructure.
b. Mitigating future City and County liability.
c. Fully leveraging and not supplanting federal or other sources.
6. INSTRUCT the CAO to report to Council on options that the City and the County may consider to accelerate completion of the disaster recovery projects.
7. INSTRUCT the CID, with the assistance of the CAO, to complete the IFP in accordance with Government Code Section 53398.63, incorporating the following terms:
a. City and County to commit no more than 50 percent of their respective shares of the tax increment for a term of up to 25 years, with final terms to be negotiated by the City and the County to support the prioritized list of projects.
b. The DRD will reimburse the City and the County for establishment costs and for staff supporting the DRD administration, financing, reporting, and funding activities.
c. All DRD public facility projects shall be completed in compliance with applicable City or County procurement processes.
d. The DRD property tax increment will be utilized on “pay-as-you-go” basis as well as security for tax increment bond issuance or loan acquisition, subject to the City Debt Management Policy, as well as any County debt policy.
e. The DRD will automatically transition to debt-service-only status upon completion of authorized projects.
f. Ability to dissolve the DRD after formation once the prioritized list of projects are completed or should other funding such as Federal Emergency Management Agency Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation, Department of Housing and Urban Development, Community Development Block Grant - Disaster Recovery be identified and the need for a DRD cease to exist, as well as ability to return any tax increment revenues to the City and the County in proportion to their respective contributions, subject to any outstanding financial obligations of the DRD.
g. Upon declaration of a fiscal emergency, the ability to suspend or reduce tax increment contribution in excess of DRD debt service or contractual obligations.
h. The final IFP and any material amendments (such as changes to the project list) shall be subject to review and approval by the City Council. B. Ad Hoc Committee for LA Recovery Report dated October 9, 2026 Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. INSTRUCT the Office of the City Administrative Officer (CAO), with the assistance of the Community Investment Department (CID) and other relevant City departments responsible for implementing potential DRD projects, to provide their report as previously instructed by Council on March 27, 2026, relative to the impact the DRD may have on Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) reimbursements in the Palisades Fire Disaster Area, including whether there are improvements or projects that can be eligible for both FEMA funds and DRD revenues. This report should be provided in 10 days, prior to the Budget and Finance Committee's consideration of the Community Investment Department’s report, dated October 5, 2026, and include the following additional analysis: (1) the percentage of tax increment to contribute to the proposed Palisades DRD; (2) prioritization of potential DRD projects; and (3) terms, contingencies, and guardrails for inclusion in the Infrastructure Financing Plan (IFP) Framework that support the Palisades recovery while preserving future property tax revenues for the General Fund and ongoing municipal services; (4) strategies and necessary IFP guardrails to fund infrastructure upgrades beyond pre-disaster conditions without jeopardizing pending FEMA Public Assistance reimbursements; (5) the legal and financial viability of utilizing DRD tax increment to reimburse the General Fund for waived rebuilding permit fees; and (6) the feasibility of establishing a dedicated funding priority or percentage set-aside for replacing low and middle-income affordable housing, including potential opportunities for acquisition, preservation and restoration of our mobile home community.
2. INSTRUCT the CID with the assistance of the CAO to complete the IFP framework outlining the proposed structure, major terms, conditions, financing parameters and other elements of the proposed DRD.
3. INSTRUCT the CID, with the assistance of the City Attorney and the CAO, to prepare a resolution of intention for potential consideration and adoption by the City Council to form the Pacific Palisades DRD, incorporating the terms, conditions, contingencies and other provisions recommended by the CAO.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
The CAO reports that the formation of a Pacific Palisades DRD will directly impact the General Fund throughout the term of the DRD as it will redirect a portion of the City‘s annual property tax revenue from the General Fund to the DRD. To preserve a portion of future property tax revenue increment for core City operational needs, the City will commit no more than 50 percent of the City’s share of tax increment from the DRD for a term of up to 25 years. With the County's participation, the tax increment revenue will be generated sooner and thereby enable the completion of recovery projects over a shorter timeframe. Additionally, implementation of the DRD will serve as key financial support for rebuilding and recovery efforts in the Pacific Palisades, spurring additional economic activity in the area that may result in additional General Fund revenues from sales taxes, business taxes, and other non- property related taxes. Financial policies The CAO reports that said CAO report is in compliance with the City’s Financial statement Policies in that, when initiating multi-year projects, the City shall consider its ability to continue to pay these future year expenses. Additionally, consistent with the City’s Financial Policies, the recommendations attempt to minimize the impact on the General Fund by ensuring other attainable funding options for projects are considered and the proposed projects are appropriately selected and evaluated. Furthermore, any issuance of debt will need to comply with the City’s Debt Management Policy.
Community Impact Statement:
Yes
